clue.text: Feverish film about year with alien

indicators.note: the film's word is wrapped about the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a pic is a film, short for picture
ET is the film alien, so a crossword stand-in for any alien

explanation.surface: A fevered movie about a year spent with a visitor from space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts YR and ET inside PIC, splitting it as P...IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyretic is the medical adjective for fever, from the Greek for fire.

clue.text: Flourish long after censure

indicators.note: the longing word is placed after the censure word

parts.note: to pan something is to criticise it harshly
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A rhetorical flourish that comes after a long telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a stylish display.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is dash or showy style, the kind of flair shown by a flourish.

clue.text: Storyteller wandering near court

indicators.note: the letters stray from their order and settle into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A storyteller roaming near the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges the letters of NEAR and COURT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone skilled at telling anecdotes and tales.

clue.text: Tense, on edge over European topic

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone tense and on edge over a European subject of debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'over' only join the pieces; in a down clue they read top to bottom in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or main idea of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Bothered to get involved

definitions.meaning: having a part or stake in an affair

explanation.surface: Someone troubled enough to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both worried and implicated, as in 'all parties concerned'.

clue.text: Fancy drink with model?

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
a model poses for an artist

explanation.surface: Would you like a drink with the model?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as 'would you like', but it is the verb meaning imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to imagine or believe it, which is to assume it is so.

clue.text: Thin wooden strip in shed

definitions.meaning: a slip of wood or paper used to light a fire
to shed is to let fall or pour out

explanation.surface: A thin strip of wood kept in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the garden hut, but it is the verb, as in shedding tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden taper for lighting fires, and also to let something pour out.

clue.text: Reigning queen as host

parts.note: the present monarch is the one now reigning
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: The queen on the throne acting as a host for guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter fronts a television or radio programme, as its host does.

clue.text: Patent from past time

parts.note: something that is over is in the past
T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A patent dating from an earlier era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like the noun for an invention licence; it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something plain to see and openly shown.

clue.text: Anne's mad about trap

indicators.note: the letters behave wildly and fall into a different order

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: Anne is furious about being caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges ANNES to ENSNA, then RE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch, as in a snare or net.

clue.text: Hotel in pleasant place that's suitable

indicators.note: the hotel letter is set inside the pleasant word

parts.note: nice means pleasant or agreeable
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel in an agreeable spot that suits the visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a position or role well suited to someone.

clue.text: Quiet isle, one disturbed by steamer

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and settle in a fresh order

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A peaceful island whose calm is broken by a passing steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges ISLE and ONE into NOISELE; 'one' is fodder here, not the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noiseless makes no sound at all, so is silent.

clue.text: Fish, for example, with number taken round in basket

indicators.note: the turned pieces are placed inside the basket word

parts.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket

indicators.note: the two pieces are turned around to read backwards

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A fish kept, along with a number of others, in a wicker basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' turns EGNO into ONGE, which 'in' sets inside CREEL after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger is a large sea eel, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Redundant old partner recalled skill

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: called back, so the skill word is read in reverse

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A former partner, now made redundant, remembers a talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses ART to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means surplus to needs, which is what redundant means.

clue.text: Master having no pawn to bring into play

indicators.note: the master word loses a letter, being without the pawn

parts.note: an expert is a master of a craft
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess master, short of a pawn, has to bring a piece into the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' takes P out of EXPERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert force or influence is to apply it or put it to use.

clue.text: Get in touch with head of embassy in attempt to expose disloyalty

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the attempt word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to reach someone is to contact them

indicators.note: the front letter of embassy is the one used

explanation.surface: Contacting the ambassador in a bid to uncover betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives E; REACH plus E goes inside TRY, making T...RY around REACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal of trust, the act of being false to one's side.

clue.text: Imminent opening of Trojan Horse, kind of horrid experience

parts.note: nigh means near at hand, about to happen

indicators.note: the first letter of Trojan is taken

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: The Trojan Horse is about to open, a frightful prospect for Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' gives T from Trojan; 'kind of' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a terrifying dream, and by extension any dreadful ordeal.

clue.text: Herb men regard curiously

indicators.note: the letters are put together in an odd, unexpected order

explanation.surface: A herb that men look at with curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges MEN and REGARD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a plant of the mint family, used in herbal remedies.

clue.text: Not accepting verdict is attractive

definitions.meaning: asking a higher court to overturn a ruling

explanation.surface: Refusing to accept the court's ruling is a charming trait.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is taking a case to a higher court; the other is being pleasing.

clue.text: One working in pub trade receiving tip

indicators.note: the trade word takes the tip word into itself

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: Someone in the pub trade being handed a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a gratuity, but it is END, which 'receiving' puts inside BARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks, working behind the bar of a pub.

clue.text: City's record during an outside broadcast brought up

indicators.note: the record sits within the other letters, in their midst
in a down clue, raised means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A record of an outside broadcast from a city, being raised in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses ANOB to BONA, and 'during' puts LOG inside, after BO. The 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Ward off disgust

explanation.surface: Fending something off out of revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is both to drive back an attacker and to cause revulsion.

clue.text: Rope, secure, holding raised beam

indicators.note: the secure word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to land something is to secure it, as a fish or a contract

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A rope that secures and holds a beam being hoisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses RAY to YAR, which 'holding' puts inside LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short cord, as on a ship or for hanging a whistle.

clue.text: So-called judge in charge is playful

parts.note: a judge is addressed as 'm'lud' in a British court, so lud is what one is called

explanation.surface: A judge, called in to take charge, turns out to be frivolous.
explanation.walkthrough: British barristers address a judge as 'my lord', slurred to 'm'lud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludic, from Latin ludus, a game, describes play and playfulness.

clue.text: Kind of wing Daedalus started with

definitions.meaning: the Greek letter that the name begins with is D

explanation.surface: Daedalus, the mythical maker of wings, began with this design.
explanation.walkthrough: Daedalus made wings in Greek myth, so the clue seems to be about his invention; but his name starts with the Greek letter for D.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta wing is triangular like the Greek capital letter, which stands for D.

clue.text: Ship's officer stole vessel loaded with most of loot

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur

indicators.note: the vessel is filled with the other letters

parts.note: a tin is a container

indicators.note: the loot word loses its last letter

parts.note: swag is stolen loot

explanation.surface: An officer stole a ship packed with most of the plunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' is the noun, a scarf, not the past of steal. 'most of' cuts SWAG to SWA, which 'loaded with' puts inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The boatswain is the ship's officer in charge of rigging, anchors and deck crew.

clue.text: Grip, say, loop in rope

indicators.note: the grip word is spoken, and a word sounding like it is written

parts.note: to bite is to grip, as a tyre bites the road

explanation.surface: Grip, for example, a loop in a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a curve or slack loop in a rope, as used in knots.

clue.text: Number in small plane

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
plane means flat or level, as even does

explanation.surface: A count of passengers on a light aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the adjective meaning flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a whole number, one more than six.

clue.text: Get led astray in mine, returning protected against collapse

indicators.note: the stray letters go inside the mine word
the mine word comes back on itself, read in reverse

parts.note: a dig is an excavation, such as a mine

indicators.note: the letters wander from their proper order

explanation.surface: Being led off course in a mine that has been shored up against collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses DIG to GID; 'astray' rearranges GETLED to LTEDGE, set in after GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt-edged securities are low-risk investments, safe from a market crash.

clue.text: See area full of natural

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'See area full of natural' (5) for VOILA: no reading of 'natural' gives the remaining letters around A for area, so a word may be misread, and no search finds the printed clue.

clue.text: Examiner puts learner in a nasty pickle

indicators.note: the learner letter is put inside the jumbled letters
being in a pickle is being in a mess, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An examiner places a student driver in an awkward fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' rearranges A NASTY; 'in' puts L inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst examines data or a patient closely, as an examiner does.

clue.text: Grass, holding info back, didn't keep promise

indicators.note: the grass word holds the reversed letters inside it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: the info word is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An informer, keeping the facts back, broke their word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' suggests a police informer, but it is REED. 'back' reverses GEN to NEG, which 'holding' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or undertaking.
